step.name: step2-rexx-dataset
step.title: Step 2: REXX Exec from Dataset (Optional)
step.description: This step shows how to execute a REXX exec stored in a dataset. This is optional because it requires a pre-existing dataset member.
step.instructions: To use a real member, create a REXX exec such as ${instance-DATASET_HLQ}.REXX(SAMPLE) and replace the inlineTemplate below with: fileTemplate -> ${instance-DATASET_HLQ}.REXX(SAMPLE) (Disabled by default - enable if you have the dataset.)

template.inlineTemplate: /* REXX */ SAY 'This is a placeholder for file-based REXX execution' SAY 'To use a dataset member, swap inlineTemplate for fileTemplate' SAY 'WORKFLOW_STEP_SUCCESS' EXIT 0

step.name: step3-inline-shell
step.title: Step 3: Inline Unix Shell Script with Variables
step.description: This step demonstrates an inline Unix shell script that accesses workflow variables, uses shell commands, and performs file operations.

template.inlineTemplate:
#!/bin/sh # Inline Shell Script Example - Variable Access and Unix Commands
echo "================================================" echo "UNIX SHELL SCRIPT - Inline Execution" echo "================================================" echo ""
# Access workflow variables using substitution USER_NAME="${instance-USER_NAME}" DATASET_HLQ="${instance-DATASET_HLQ}" COUNTER=${instance-COUNTER}
echo "Input Variables:" echo " USER_NAME = $USER_NAME" echo " DATASET_HLQ = $DATASET_HLQ" echo " COUNTER = $COUNTER" echo ""
# Perform some operations NEW_COUNTER=$((COUNTER + 20)) TIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') MESSAGE="Hello $USER_NAME from shell! Counter is now $NEW_COUNTER"
echo "Processing:" echo " New Counter = $NEW_COUNTER" echo " Timestamp = $TIMESTAMP" echo " Message = $MESSAGE" echo ""
# Demonstrate Unix commands echo "Unix Environment Information:" echo " Hostname = $(hostname)" echo " Current User = $(whoami)" echo " Current Dir = $(pwd)" echo " Home Dir = $HOME" echo ""
# File operations example TEMP_FILE="/tmp/workflow_test_$$" echo "Creating temporary file: $TEMP_FILE" echo "Workflow test data" > "$TEMP_FILE" echo "Counter: $NEW_COUNTER" >> "$TEMP_FILE" echo "User: $USER_NAME" >> "$TEMP_FILE"
if [ -f "$TEMP_FILE" ]; then echo "File created successfully. Contents:" cat "$TEMP_FILE" echo "" rm "$TEMP_FILE" echo "Temporary file removed." else echo "Warning: File creation failed" fi echo ""
echo "Shell script execution completed successfully!" echo "================================================"
exit 0

step.name: step5b-shell-advanced
step.title: Step 5 (cont.): Shell Advanced Variable Handling
step.description: Advanced shell techniques: string manipulation, arithmetic, conditional logic, and parameter expansion (POSIX /bin/sh).
step.instructions: Shell script demonstrating advanced variable manipulation.

template.inlineTemplate:
#!/bin/sh echo "================================================" echo "SHELL ADVANCED VARIABLE TECHNIQUES" echo "================================================" echo ""
# Get variables USER_NAME="${instance-USER_NAME}" COUNTER=${instance-COUNTER}
# String manipulation # NOTE: avoid shell brace parameter-expansion (length, default-value, substring # forms) here. With substitution=true the z/OSMF template engine parses EVERY # dollar-brace token as a workflow variable - even inside shell comments - and # fails on shell-specific syntax (IZUWF0084E). Use plain $VAR for workflow # values and brace-free constructs for everything else. NAME_LEN=$(printf %s "$USER_NAME" | wc -c | tr -d ' ') echo "String Manipulation:" echo " Original name: $USER_NAME" echo " Uppercase: $(echo $USER_NAME | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')" echo " Lowercase: $(echo $USER_NAME | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" echo " Length: $NAME_LEN" echo ""
# Numeric operations echo "Numeric Operations:" echo " Counter: $COUNTER" echo " Counter + 5: $((COUNTER + 5))" echo " Counter * 3: $((COUNTER * 3))" echo " Counter / 2: $((COUNTER / 2))" echo " Counter % 3: $((COUNTER % 3))" echo ""
# Conditional logic echo "Conditional Logic:" if [ $COUNTER -gt 10 ]; then echo " Counter is greater than 10" else echo " Counter is 10 or less" fi
if [ "$NAME_LEN" -gt 5 ]; then echo " Name is longer than 5 characters" else echo " Name is 5 characters or shorter" fi echo ""
# Iterating a list (POSIX-portable, no bash arrays) echo "List Iteration:" i=0 OLDIFS=$IFS IFS='|' for item in "First item|Second item|Third item"; do set -- $item for x in "$@"; do echo " item[$i] = $x" i=$((i + 1)) done done IFS=$OLDIFS echo ""
# Default value (brace-free; a shell default-value expansion would break # z/OSMF substitution, so test for empty explicitly instead) echo "Default Value Handling:" VAR="Hello World" echo " Original: $VAR" DEFVAL=$UNDEFINED_VAR if [ -z "$DEFVAL" ]; then DEFVAL="default"; fi echo " Default value: $DEFVAL" echo ""
echo "Advanced shell techniques demonstrated!" echo "================================================"
exit 0

step.name: step6-summary
step.title: Step 6: Summary and Next Steps
step.description: Review what was learned and suggestions for further exploration.
step.instructions:
Congratulations, ${instance-USER_NAME}! You've completed the workflow.
You've learned: 1. How to create inline REXX exec steps 2. How to create inline Unix shell script steps 3. How to pass variables using substitution 4. How to reference file-based scripts (fileTemplate) 5. Advanced variable manipulation techniques
Key Concepts: - A step action is one of: template, rest, setVariable. There is NO rexx, shell, unixShell or inline element in the z/OSMF schema - A step with weight/skills/autoEnable/canMarkAsFailed is a leaf and must be followed by an action; it cannot also contain substeps - Use substitution="true" to enable variable substitution - Variables are accessed as the dollar-brace VARIABLE_NAME form - REXX runs via a template element using submitAs TSO-REXX, plus a required successPattern (success is judged from stdout) - Shell runs via a template element using submitAs shell-JCL, with NO successPattern (it runs as a BPXBATCH job, judged by RC) - inlineTemplate holds the script; fileTemplate names a dataset/USS file - CDATA sections prevent XML parsing of script content
Next Steps: - Try modifying the scripts with your own logic - Create file-based scripts and switch to fileTemplate - Experiment with different variable types - Explore JCL steps for comparison
